before.title: Periodic responses of $\ddot z=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ and the affine classification of all solutions
before.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the weak-field Thomson item (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
before.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $T:=2\pi/\omega$, $n\ge1$ and $w\in\mathbb C^n$; use the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]]. Define $z_p:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ by $z_p(t):=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-derivative]] for the derivative below). Then: (a) $z_p$ is $C^\infty$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and satisfies $z_p''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$; it is $T$-periodic. (b) every $C^2$ solution $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ of $z''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ on $\mathbb R$ has the form $z(t)=z_p(t)+a+bt$ with unique $a,b\in\mathbb R^n$. (c) such a solution is $T$-periodic if and only if $b=0$; the $T$-periodic solutions are exactly $z_p(t)+a$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$, and their oscillating part has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$.
before.strategy: (a) By the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $z_p(t)=-\omega^{-2}[(\operatorname{Re}w)\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w)\sin(\omega t)]$ componentwise. Differentiating twice with the sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and the derivatives of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] gives $z_p''=\operatorname{Re}w\cos(\omega t)+\operatorname{Im}w\sin(\omega t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$. Periodicity of $z_p$ follows from $e^{-i\omega(t+T)}=e^{-i\omega t}e^{-i\omega T}=e^{-i\omega t}$ by the addition law of [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]] and $e^{-2\pi i}=1$, the latter from the Cartesian form and the values $\cos2\pi=1$, $\sin2\pi=0$ of [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]]. (b) If $z$ is any $C^2$ solution, then $h:=z-z_p$ satisfies $h''=0$ on $\mathbb R$. Apply [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] on the interval $\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) to each component of $h'$: $h'=b$ is constant. Applying the same corollary to $h-b\,\mathrm{id}$ gives $h=z_p+a+bt$. Uniqueness of $a,b$ from $z(0)$ and $z'(0)$ is immediate. (c) If $b=0$ then $z=z_p+a$ is $T$-periodic by (a). Conversely, if $z$ is $T$-periodic then $z(t+T)-z(t)=bT$ for all $t$, hence $b=0$; then $z-z_p=a$ is the constant part whose complex amplitude is zero, while the oscillating part $z_p$ has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$ by construction. No choice principle is used.

before.title: The ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model
before.reference: scaffold-added necessary model definition for the dipole scattering and Thomson items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
before.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $k:=\omega/c$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\mu_0>0$ the vacuum permeability of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$ (the complex dipole-moment amplitude, in $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m$). Define, on the punctured space $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ and all times $t\in\mathbb R$, $$E_{\rm d}(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(-\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}\,n\times(n\times p_0)\,e^{i(kr-\omega t)}\Bigr),\qquad B_{\rm d}(x,t):=\frac1c\,n\times E_{\rm d}(x,t),$$ where $r:=|x|$ and $n:=x/r$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), with the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]] and the real-field encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]. Call $(E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d})$ the **ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of frequency $\omega$ and amplitude $p_0$**, and call $S_{\rm d}:=E_{\rm d}\times B_{\rm d}/\mu_0$ its model flux ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]); the model fields are read as an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]]. [Adopted status] This is an explicitly adopted ideal radiation-law model, fixed by the following declarations: (i) it is the leading transverse far-zone field of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) evaluated at the harmonic transverse moment $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, i.e. at $p''$ for the waveform $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$; (ii) the model contains no independent magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole radiation, no near-zone or static field and no other radiating component; (iii) it is not asserted to solve the vacuum Maxwell equations at finite $r$, to be the field of any actual source, to satisfy any boundary condition or to have finite total energy on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$; (iv) for compact smooth conserved sources the difference from the actual retarded fields is controlled only by the explicit absolute bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]]. No measured, empirical or material-response content is adopted: $p_0$ is prescribed model data, not a derived polarizability.
before.strategy: This is a definition contract; well-definedness is discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) The formula is the leading transverse term $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$ of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) at $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$: since $p''(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$ for $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, the complex derivative being the one of [[def-complex-exponential]], the model field is exactly $E_{\rm lead}$ rewritten with $u=t-r/c$ and $e^{i(kr-\omega t)}=e^{-i\omega(t-r/c)}$; the cross product, inner product and norm are those of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] and [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. (ii) $r>0$ on the declared domain, so $E_{\rm d}$ and $B_{\rm d}$ are $C^\infty$ there and the real-part encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] applies; $E_{\rm d}\cdot n=0$ because $n\times(n\times p_0)$ is orthogonal to $n$, and $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ by definition. (iii) The model flux $S_{\rm d}$ is the quantity of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] evaluated at the model fields; that definition applies to any pair of fields of the declared regularity and assigns no field equation. (iv) The status clause lists the model assumptions (i)-(iv) and excludes exact Maxwell, source-realization, boundary, finite-energy and empirical claims; the model's relation to actual sources is only through the explicit bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], which are quantified in the item below. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Differential and total cross sections of the ideal harmonic dipole in a plane-wave field
before.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the period-average and cross-section algebra itself uses no choice. Adopt the ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of [[def-em-ideal-harmonic-dipole-model]] with frequency $\omega>0$, wavenumber $k=\omega/c$ and amplitude $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$; let $E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d},S_{\rm d}$ be its fields and model flux. Let $\kappa\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, $e\in\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b:=\kappa\times e/\omega$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and let $(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ be the corresponding plane-wave fields of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$; by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] they satisfy the smooth-branch source-free vacuum Maxwell equations, and by [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b) their period-averaged energy flux has magnitude $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). Define the **model differential scattering cross section** by $$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n):=\frac{r^2\langle S_{\rm d}(rn,\cdot)\cdot n\rangle}{\langle S_{\rm inc}\cdot\hat\kappa\rangle},\qquad n\in S^2,\ r>0,$$ where $\hat\kappa:=\kappa/|\kappa|$, $S_{\rm inc}:=E_{\rm inc}\times B_{\rm inc}/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]), and $\langle f\rangle:=\frac1T\int_0^Tf(s)\,ds$, $T=2\pi/\omega$, is the period average at fixed observation point. Then: (a) [Angular pattern] the ratio is independent of $r$ and of the averaging start, and for every $n\in S^2$ $$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2|e|^2}.$$ (b) [Total cross section] with $d\sigma_{S^2}$ the surface measure of the unit sphere, $\sigma:=\int_{S^2}\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}\,d\sigma_{S^2}$ equals $$\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2};$$ if $p_0=\alpha e$ for a complex scalar $\alpha$ (the scalar polarizability, in $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$), then $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ and $\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4}|n\times\hat e|^2$ with $\hat e:=e/|e|$. (c) [Fidelity to the compact-source dipole theorem] the model field is exactly the leading transverse field $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$ of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) evaluated at the harmonic transverse moment $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$. Consequently, for an actual source of that theorem's class, the difference between its retarded field at $(rn,u+r/c)$ and the model field is bounded by $\Gamma_E/r^2+\mu_0D(u)/(2\pi r)$ in the electric field and by $(\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c)/r^2$ plus $c^{-1}$ times that bound in the magnetic field, uniformly in $n$, where $D(u)$ is that theorem's explicit source-variation bound ([[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](b)-(c)); no smallness of $D(u)$ is asserted. (d) [Scope] conditional predictions of the adopted ideal model: no measured cross section, no frequency-domain response law (the amplitude $p_0$ is prescribed model data), no magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole content, no self-force, material response, finite-size or empirical claim; the scalar-$\alpha$ clause records a declared proportional response, not a derived polarizability.
before.strategy: (a) In the model, $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ and $n\cdot E_{\rm d}=0$, so $S_{\rm d}\cdot n=n\cdot(E_{\rm d}\times(n\times E_{\rm d}))/(\mu_0c)=|E_{\rm d}|^2/(\mu_0c)$ pointwise; writing $w:=\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p_0)e^{ikr}$, the model has $E_{\rm d}=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$, and [[lem-em-period-average]] gives $\langle|E_{\rm d}|^2\rangle=\frac12|w|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{32\pi^2r^2}|n\times p_0|^2$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). Hence $r^2\langle S_{\rm d}\cdot n\rangle=\frac{\mu_0\omega^4}{32\pi^2c}|n\times p_0|^2$, independent of $r$ and of the averaging start. Division by the incident flux $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ of [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b) and $\mu_0^2=\frac1{\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]) give the two displayed forms. after.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the period-average and cross-section algebra itself uses no choice. Adopt the ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of [[def-em-ideal-harmonic-dipole-model]] with frequency $\omega>0$, wavenumber $k=\omega/c$ and amplitude $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$; let $E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d},S_{\rm d}$ be its fields and model flux. Let $\kappa\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, $e\in\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b:=\kappa\times e/\omega$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and let $(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ be the corresponding plane-wave fields of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$; by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] they satisfy the smooth-branch source-free vacuum Maxwell equations, and by [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b) their period-averaged energy flux has magnitude $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). Define the **model differential scattering cross section** by $$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n):=\frac{r^2\langle S_{\rm d}(rn,\cdot)\cdot n\rangle}{\langle S_{\rm inc}\cdot\hat\kappa\rangle},\qquad n\in S^2,\ r>0,$$ where $\hat\kappa:=\kappa/|\kappa|$, $S_{\rm inc}:=E_{\rm inc}\times B_{\rm inc}/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]), and $\langle f\rangle:=\frac1T\int_0^Tf(s)\,ds$, $T=2\pi/\omega$, is the period average at fixed observation point. Then: (a) [Angular pattern] the ratio is independent of $r$ and of the averaging start, and for every $n\in S^2$ $$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2|e|^2}.$$ (b) [Total cross section] with $d\sigma_{S^2}$ the surface measure of the unit sphere, $\sigma:=\int_{S^2}\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}\,d\sigma_{S^2}$ equals $$\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2};$$ if $p_0=\alpha e$ for a complex scalar $\alpha$ (the scalar polarizability, in $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$), then $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ and $\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4}|n\times\hat e|^2$ with $\hat e:=e/|e|$. (c) [Fidelity for arbitrary actual sources and matched windows] Let an actual compact smooth conserved source satisfy the exact hypotheses of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], with spatial support radius a>0, source-time interval [tau0,tau1], moment p_act(u), variation bound D(u) and constants Gamma_E,Gamma_B. These source data are independent of the prescribed model amplitude p0. Put
$$p_h(u):=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u}),\qquad M(u):=|p_{\rm act}''(u)-p_h''(u)|.$$
For n in S2,u in[tau0,tau1],r>=2a, define
$$H(u,r):=\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}[D(u)+M(u)].$$
The actual retarded fields and the model fields satisfy, uniformly in n,
$$|E_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-E_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)|\le H(u,r),$$
$$|B_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-B_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}+\frac{H(u,r)}c.$$
Also retain the sharper direct source-leading-field consequence
$$|B_{\rm act}-B_{\rm d}|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0[D(u)+M(u)]}{4\pi cr}$$
at the same events. If p_act''=p_h'' on a specified finite window, M0 there and these give the full matched dipole bounds; in particular they imply the older coarser electric bound Gamma_E/r²+mu0 D/(2pi r). Neither moment matching nor D0 is automatic. A sound sufficient matched branch is p_act=p_h+a0+b0 u on an open neighborhood of the window (any fixed real vectors a0,b0). Such a branch has actual compact realizations over any finite window: choose a smooth time cutoff eta equal1 near the window, let p_eta=eta(p_h+a0+b0 u), choose a nonnegative smooth spatial bump sigma with support inside B_a and integral1, and set rho=-p_eta dot grad sigma,J=p_eta' sigma. Then continuity holds and the actual moment is p_eta; outside the window it is tapered. Apply the actual theorem with the resulting D and Gamma, retaining every finite-radius/source-variation error. No eternal harmonic moment of a compact-time source is asserted. (d) [Scope] conditional predictions of the adopted ideal model: no measured cross section, no frequency-domain response law (the amplitude $p_0$ is prescribed model data), no magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole content, no self-force, material response, finite-size or empirical claim; the scalar-$\alpha$ clause records a declared proportional response, not a derived polarizability. In all complex-amplitude formulas |v|²=sum_i |v_i|² is the Hermitian norm square; n cross v is complex-linear for real n. The p0=0 case gives zero scattered fields and cross sections while the nonzero incident intensity still defines the ratios. Actual-source fidelity assumes only the explicitly quantified mismatch and source hypotheses; it does not turn the model cross section into a measured or self-consistent scattering prediction.
after.strategy: (a) In the model, $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ and $n\cdot E_{\rm d}=0$, so $S_{\rm d}\cdot n=n\cdot(E_{\rm d}\times(n\times E_{\rm d}))/(\mu_0c)=|E_{\rm d}|^2/(\mu_0c)$ pointwise; writing $w:=-\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p_0)e^{ikr}$, the model has $E_{\rm d}=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$, and [[lem-em-period-average]] gives $\langle|E_{\rm d}|^2\rangle=\frac12|w|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{32\pi^2r^2}|n\times p_0|^2$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). (b) [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d) gives $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=\frac{8\pi}3|a|^2$ for real $a$, and applying it to the real and imaginary parts of $p_0$ gives the complex case; integrating the pattern of (a) over $S^2$ yields $\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{16\pi^2|e|^2}\cdot\frac{8\pi}3|p_0|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2}$, i.e. the two displayed forms. For $p_0=\alpha e$ substitute $|p_0|^2=|\alpha|^2|e|^2$ and $|n\times p_0|^2=|\alpha|^2|e|^2|n\times\hat e|^2$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). (c) At t=u+r/c the SIGNED model leading field is mu0 n cross(n cross p_h''(u))/(4pi r). The actual source theorem bounds E_act against the leading field of p_act'' by Gamma_E/r²+mu0 D/(4pi r). The real unit-direction double-cross projection has norm at most1, so the difference of the two leading fields is bounded by mu0 M/(4pi r). Adding gives H, including the zero actual source countercheck: then D=Gamma0 but M=|p_h''|, which exactly accounts for a nonzero prescribed model. The source theorem's B-n cross E_act/c bound is (Gamma_B+Gamma_E/c)/r²; add c^-1 times H to obtain the retained magnetic bound. Separately its stronger B-leading(V_act) estimate is Gamma_B/r²; |V_act-p_h''|<=D+M gives the sharper direct magnetic estimate. For the compact-window construction, smooth nonnegative cutoffs from [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]] may be normalized and scaled to give sigma ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]] for the scaling convention). Continuity is rho_t=-p_eta' dot grad sigma and div J=p_eta' dot grad sigma. Integration by parts on a bounding rectangle gives integral rho0 and integral y_i rho=(p_eta)_i integral sigma=(p_eta)_i, using [[thm-integration-by-parts]], [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] and the Countable-Choice comparison [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]. Choose source-time endpoints outside the taper support, so all compact smooth hypotheses are met. Moment matching on the window removes M, but D and Gamma remain the actual finite-source quantities. (d) records the scope; no measured or material content is added ([[def-em-si-conventions]] only fixes units and constants). No choice principle beyond that carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] (Countable Choice, as stated there) is used. The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the actual compact-source and sphere-moment suppliers; the finite period-average calculation and cross-section algebra are choice-free. Complex norms mean |v|²=sum_i |v_i|². Real unit n acts complex-linearly by cross products; all norm identities used in(a),(b) follow by summing the real and imaginary norm identities. The minus sign in w agrees with the model definition; squaring for its flux does not erase a sign mismatch in the field identity. Period averaging adds no choice; Countable Choice here is precisely the actual source/sphere-integral premise.

before.title: Controlled first variation of the relativistic test-charge law: the leading Thomson-model cross section
before.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]]; the linearization below and [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]] use no choice. Assume the setting and postulates of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] for a test particle with charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-sources]](a)) and externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, in the incident plane-wave field of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with wavevector $\kappa$, complex amplitude $e\ne0$, $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $|\kappa|=\omega/c$ and $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ as in [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]]; write $E_{\rm inc}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x-\omega t)})$ and $B_{\rm inc}=\kappa\times E_{\rm inc}/\omega$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Assume that for some $\eta_0>0$ and a common open interval $I\ni0$, for every $\eta\in(-\eta_0,\eta_0)$ there is a $C^2$ future timelike massive solution $r_\eta:I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the adopted four-force law in the external field $\eta(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ (no self-field, recoil or material force), and that the family admits a uniform first-order expansion: there are $r_1\in C^2(I;\mathbb R^3)$ and, for every compact $K\subset I$, a constant $C_K$ with $$|r_\eta(t)-x_0-\eta r_1(t)|+|\dot r_\eta(t)-\eta\dot r_1(t)|\le C_K\eta^2\qquad(t\in K,\ |\eta|\le\eta_0)$$ about a fixed position $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, and the first-order displacement $z_1:=r_1$ is $T$-periodic, $T=2\pi/\omega$. Then: (a) [Linearized equation] $\ddot r_1(t)=\frac qmE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)=\frac qm\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x_0-\omega t)})$ on $I$. (b) [Induced dipole] with $x_0$ the particle's mean position, the oscillating part of the first-order dipole moment $q(r_1-z_1^{\rm mean})$ is $\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega t})$ with complex amplitude $$p_0=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}\,e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0};$$ equivalently $p_0=\alpha e'$ with $\alpha=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}$ (units $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$) and the unimodular factor $e'=e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, $|e'|=|e|$. (c) [Leading Thomson-model cross section] substituting this $p_0$ into [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]](b) gives $$\sigma_{\rm T}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}=\frac{8\pi}{3}\Bigl(\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0mc^2}\Bigr)^2,$$ independent of $\omega$ and of the phase factor. (d) [Scope] this is a controlled conditional first variation of the adopted relativistic external-force law under the stated solution-family hypotheses. It is not the exact Newtonian force postulate, it does not assert existence, persistence, stability or self-consistency of the family, it excludes self-force, radiation reaction and material media, and it makes no empirical, measurement, atomic-physics or frequency-response claim.
before.strategy: The proof is the $\eta\to0$ linearization of the coordinate form of the adopted four-force law, followed by the periodic-response lemma and the substitution into the cross-section theorem. (i) Along the family, [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]](a) gives $m\frac{d}{dt}(\gamma_\eta\dot r_\eta)=q\eta(E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta,t)+\dot r_\eta\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta,t))$. By the expansion, $|\dot r_\eta|=O(\eta)$ uniformly on each compact $K$, so clause (c) of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] with fixed $\delta$ gives $\gamma_\eta=1+O(\eta^2)$. Hence $m\frac{d}{dt}(\gamma_\eta\dot r_\eta)=m\ddot r_\eta+O(\eta^2)=m\eta\ddot r_1+O(\eta^2)$; the magnetic term is $q\eta\dot r_\eta\times B_{\rm inc}=O(\eta^2)$; and the electric term is $q\eta E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta,t)=q\eta E_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)+O(\eta^2)$ because $E_{\rm inc}$ is smooth and $r_\eta-x_0=O(\eta)$ uniformly on $K$. Dividing by $\eta$ and letting $\eta\to0$ gives (a). (ii) By (a) and [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]](b)-(c) with $w=\frac qme e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, the $T$-periodic $r_1$ equals $\operatorname{Re}(-\frac q{m\omega^2}e e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}e^{-i\omega t})+a$; subtracting its mean $a$, the oscillating displacement has complex amplitude $-\frac q{m\omega^2}e e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, so the oscillating dipole moment $q(r_1-a)$ has amplitude $p_0=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}e e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$; the phase factor is unimodular, so $|p_0|=\frac{q^2|e|}{m\omega^2}$ and $p_0=\alpha e'$ with $\alpha=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}$, $|e'|=|e|$. (iii) Inserting $p_0=\alpha e'$ into [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]](b) gives $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}$, and the parenthesis is $\frac{8\pi}3r_q^2$ with $r_q=\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0mc^2}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]] for the constants). (iv) No choice principle is used here: the linearization is finite-dimensional calculus, the periodic-response lemma is choice-free, and the cross-section substitution is algebra; the Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the cross-section theorem being substituted into.

Their squared flux factors eta² cancel in its cross-section ratio; sigma_T is this leading-model coefficient, not an assertion of the exact nonlinear particle's emitted field or cross section. Use the exact integrated momentum ODE; never differentiate a uniform-in-time Oeta² remainder. Fix a compact K in I and choose a closed interval L contained in I that contains K and0. Put v_eta=r_eta', gamma_eta=(1-|v_eta|²/c²)^-1/2, and P_eta=m gamma_eta v_eta. The stated family expansion implies r_eta->x0 and v_eta/eta->r1' uniformly on L as eta->0 with eta!=0, and |v_eta|=O(|eta|). For small eta the fixed speed bound |v_eta|/c<=1/2 holds on L; the actual algebraic low-speed clause of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] gives gamma_eta=1+O(eta²) uniformly. Hence P_eta/eta->m r1' uniformly, using only multiplication of uniformly bounded functions.
The EXACT coordinate ODE of that supplier is
$$P_\eta'(t)=q\eta\,[E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)+v_\eta(t)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)].$$
The plane-wave fields are smooth with bounded spatial first derivatives on a common compact tube around x0 times L, so their values at r_eta converge uniformly to their values at x0; the magnetic term is uniformly Oeta since B is bounded and v_eta=Oeta. Thus for eta!=0, P_eta'/eta converges uniformly to q E_inc(x0,t). This derivative convergence comes from the adopted ODE, not from differentiating the family expansion. Apply componentwise scalar FTC [[thm-ftc-second-part]] to the actual C1 momentum on [0,t], with oriented limits for t<0:
$$\frac{P_\eta(t)-P_\eta(0)}\eta=q\int_0^t[E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(s),s)+v_\eta(s)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(s),s)]ds.$$
Uniform convergence passes through these finite ordinary integrals: each component's error is at most the interval length times its uniform supremum, by [[lem-integral-elementary-bounds]]. Taking the limit gives
$$m[r_1'(t)-r_1'(0)]=q\int_0^tE_{\rm inc}(x_0,s)ds.$$
The continuous integrand and [[thm-ftc-first-part]] now imply m r1''=q E_inc(x0,t) on I. This proves(a) and the available first-order equation while retaining the original position/velocity assumptions and arbitrary local I; no differentiability in eta beyond the given uniform expansion and no acceleration-error differentiation is assumed. The parameter endpoints eta=+-eta0 are never evaluated. A continuous differentiable family was not replaced by a stronger C2-in-eta family.
By the LOCAL interval/global extension clause(d) of [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]] with w=(q/m)e exp(i kappa dot x0), r1=z_p+a+bt on I and its explicit extension on R is unique. Preparation(P) says this extension is periodic, hence b0; this is nonvacuous even when I is shorter than a period. Its mean a comes from the harmonic lemma's finite-period mean calculation. Therefore q(r1-a)=Re[-q² e exp(i kappa dot x0) exp(-i omega t)/(m omega²)], proving(b), with the arbitrary constant mean retained and x0 only the zeroth-order reference position. The phase factor has modulus1 by [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], so |p0|=q²|e|/(m omega²) and p0=alpha e', alpha=-q²/(m omega²).
Substituting into [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]](b) cancels omega^4 and gives sigma_T=q^4/(6pi epsilon0²m²c^4)=(8pi/3)[q²/(4pi epsilon0 m c²)]². At q0 the same algebra gives zero response amplitude and zero cross section. Finite-interval FTC, uniform limits and harmonic affine classification are choice-free; only the stated cross-section source/sphere premise carries Countable Choice.

current_object.title: Controlled electric-dipole far field and retarded-time radiated power of a compact smooth source
current_object.statement: Assume the setting and hypotheses of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by its suppliers: $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $a>0$, $t_0<T$, jointly $C^\infty$ fields $\rho,J$ vanishing outside $\overline B_a(0)\times[t_0,T]$ and satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$; let $\varphi,A$ be the retarded potentials and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ the fields, with $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Adopt the causal selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]]: these retarded fields are the fields of the source model (the compact smooth instance established by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]). Define the **time-dependent electric dipole moment** $$p(u):=\int_{B_a}y\,\rho(y,u)\,dy\in\mathbb R^3$$ (componentwise, about the fixed chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; it is the fixed-time analogue of the static source moment of [[def-em-electric-moments]]), and, as in the asymptotic theorem, $I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$, $V(n,u):=\partial_uI(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$ and $$D(u):=\frac{a}{c}\int_{B_a}\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|\,dy.$$ Then: (a) [Moment identities] $p\in C^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^3)$, $p'(u)=\int_{B_a}J(y,u)\,dy$, $p''(u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u)\,dy$, $\int_{B_a}\rho_t(y,u)\,dy=0$ and the total charge $\int_{B_a}\rho(y,u)\,dy$ vanishes for every $u$. (b) [Dipole replacement error] $|V(n,u)-p''(u)|\le D(u)$ for every $n\in S^2$ and every $u\in[t_0,T]$: the explicit absolute error of the dipole approximation to the source's transverse current moment. (c) [Leading fields] With $\Gamma_E$, $\Gamma_B$ the constants of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](b) (depending only on $a,c,\mu_0$ and the listed source suprema), for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in[t_0,T]$, $r\ge2a$: $$\Bigl|E\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p''(u))\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D(u)}{4\pi r},\qquad \Bigl|B\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{n\times E(rn,u+\tfrac rc)}{c}\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}.$$ The leading far field is the electric-dipole field, with amplitude proportional to $p''(u)$; all errors are uniform in the direction $n$ at fixed $u$. (d) [Retarded-time radiated power] The limit of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](c) equals $\mu_0|p''(u)|^2/(6\pi c)+R(u)$ with the explicit absolute error $$|R(u)|\le\frac{\mu_0\bigl(2|p''(u)|D(u)+D(u)^2\bigr)}{4\pi c},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0}{6\pi c}|p''(u)|^2\ \text{ whenever } D(u)=0.$$ The evaluation uses the sphere moment $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$ of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d). The limit is at fixed retarded time $u$, not at fixed observation time. (e) [Scope] The compact smooth source branch only; the dipole error is absolute and explicitly controlled by $D(u)$, and no assertion is made that slow or 'nonrelativistic' source motion alone makes $D(u)$ small -- that is a hypothesis on the source's time variation. No point charge, no moving point source, no radiation reaction, no self-force and no empirical or measurement content; the failure of the correspondence with an oscillator for rapidly varying sources is retained through $D(u)$. Separately retain the sharper actual source estimate $|B(rn,u+r/c)-n\times E_{\rm lead}(n,u,r)/c|\le\Gamma_B/r^2$, with $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$; the bound against the actual E uses the combined constant displayed in(c).
current_object.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]]. (a) $\rho$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, so $u\mapsto p(u)$ is $C^\infty$ by differentiation under the integral sign ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]) and $p'(u)=\int y\,\rho_t(y,u)dy$; integrating by parts componentwise over a ball containing the support via the divergence theorem ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]], boundary term zero by compact support) gives $\int y_i\partial_t\rho\,dy=-\int y_i\operatorname{div}J\,dy=\int J_i\,dy$, since $\partial_i(y_iJ_k)$ contributes $J_i$ and the remaining divergence term integrates to zero. Replacing $J$ by $J_t$ (equivalently differentiating in $u$ under the integral sign) gives $p''=\int J_t$. The vanishing $\int\rho_t=0$ is the same divergence theorem with weight $1$ (equivalently clause (f) of [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]), and the total charge vanishes because $\rho$ is supported in $t\in[t_0,T]$. (b) For fixed $y\in B_a$ the one-variable function $v\mapsto J_t(y,v)$ is $C^1$ on the interval between $u$ and $u+n\cdot y/c$, whose length is at most $a/c$; for nonzero vector difference w choose its fixed unit direction e=w/|w| and apply the scalar mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]) to e dot J_t; finite Euclidean Cauchy-Schwarz bounds |e dot J_tt| by |J_tt| (the zero difference is immediate), giving $|J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)-J_t(y,u)|\le(a/c)\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|$ componentwise, and integrating over $B_a$ with the integral triangle inequality and monotonicity ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) gives (b). (c) Clause (b) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] writes $E(rn,u+r/c)=E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)+$ remainder with $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0\,n\times(n\times V(n,u))/(4\pi r)$ and remainder $O(r^{-2})$ bounded by $\Gamma_E r^{-2}$. Substituting $V=p''+(V-p'')$ and using $|n\times(n\times w)|\le|w|$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]) gives the first bound; The supplier bounds B-n cross E_lead/c by Gamma_B/r² and E-E_lead by Gamma_E/r²; the triangle inequality therefore gives the displayed (Gamma_B+Gamma_E/c)/r² bound against the actual E. D=0 suffices for exact dipole power; no converse is inferred from an error bound. (d) By clause (c) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] the limit equals $\mu_0/(16\pi^2c)\int_{S^2}|n\times V|^2d\sigma$. Replacing $V$ by $p''$ changes the integrand by at most $(2|p''|D+D^2)$ pointwise (expand $|n\times V|^2-|n\times p''|^2$ and use the bound (b), the linearity of the cross product and the integral triangle inequality), so the integral changes by at most $4\pi(2|p''|D+D^2)$ and the limit by $\mu_0(2|p''|D+D^2)/(4\pi c)$. The exact dipole value uses $|n\times p''|^2=|p''|^2-(n\cdot p'')^2$ and clause (d) of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]]: $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=4\pi|p''|^2-(4\pi/3)|p''|^2=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$, and $\mu_0/(16\pi^2c)\cdot(8\pi/3)=\mu_0/(6\pi c)$. (e) records that the error coefficient $D(u)$ constrains the source's own time variation and that the limit is a fixed-retarded-time limit, as in the supplier; no self-force, point-source, decay or empirical claim is added.

current_object.title: Harmonic dipole pattern and period-averaged power in the exact dipole law
current_object.statement: Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the surface and finite-source branches. Adopt the electric-dipole radiation-law idealization whose leading far fields and angular flux are the dipole expressions of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], evaluated for the prescribed smooth waveform p(u)=p0 cos(omega u)e3 with omega>0 and p0!=0. This is an explicit ideal radiation-law model, not an eternal compact-time source claimed to satisfy that theorem with D0. The waveform is a moment convention of [[def-em-electric-moments]], not measured data. All exact quantities below refer to that ideal leading radiation law. Then: (a) [Fields] With $n=\sin\theta\cos\varphi\,e_1+\sin\theta\sin\varphi\,e_2+\cos\theta\,e_3$, $\theta\in[0,\pi]$, the leading far fields are $$E_{\mathrm{lead}}(rn,u+r/c)=-\frac{\mu_0\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)}{4\pi r}\,n\times(n\times e_3),\qquad B_{\mathrm{lead}}=\frac{n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}}{c},$$ with $|n\times(n\times e_3)|=\sin\theta$, so the amplitude pattern is $\propto\sin\theta$ and vanishes on the dipole axis $\theta\in\{0,\pi\}$. (b) [Angular power density] The retarded-time angular power density of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] is $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n,u)=\frac{\mu_0|n\times p''(u)|^{2}}{16\pi^{2}c}=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{16\pi^{2}c}\,\sin^{2}\theta,$$ the $\sin^{2}\theta$ pattern with zeros along $\pm e_3$ and maximum in the equatorial plane; its integral over the sphere is $$\int_{S^2}\frac{dP}{d\sigma}d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c},$$ using $\int_{S^2}\sin^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=8\pi/3$ from [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](a). (c) [Period average] The mean of the total power over one retarded-time period $u\in[0,2\pi/\omega]$ is $$\frac{\omega}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi/\omega}\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c}\,du=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}}{12\pi c}.$$ (d) [Scope] The computation is the exact dipole law of the model; a finite prescribed source realizes it only within the absolute error bound of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] with its $D(u)$, and a physical antenna's feed, current distribution and material realization are additional source models not supplied here. The average in (c) is taken in the retarded-time variable, not in observation time; no measurement, radiation resistance, matching condition or effective area is reported, and no empirical claim is made. (e) [Actual compact-window realization] Choose a compact smooth time cutoff eta equal1 near one selected period, a nonnegative C-infinity bump sigma supported in B_a with integral1, and p_eta(u)=eta(u)p0 cos(omega u)e3. Define rho(y,u)=-p_eta(u) dot grad sigma(y), J(y,u)=p_eta'(u)sigma(y). These are smooth compact spacetime sources, satisfy continuity, carry zero total charge and have moment p_eta. On the chosen period the moment equals the harmonic waveform, while the ACTUAL retarded field has the full D(u),Gamma_E/r² and (Gamma_B+Gamma_E/c)/r² errors of the dipole theorem. Its asymptotic total-power deviation from the ideal law is bounded by that theorem's explicit R(u); its period-averaged deviation is bounded by the average of |R(u)|. V=p'' is a sufficient ideal transverse-moment condition; it is not equivalent to D0. No eternal nonzero harmonic moment is asserted for a compact-time source.
current_object.strategy: Direct substitution in [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]]. (a) $p(u)=p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ gives $p''(u)=-\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives|the scalar multiple rule]]), and clause (c) of the theorem gives $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0\,n\times(n\times p'')/(4\pi r)$ with $B_{\mathrm{lead}}=n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}/c$ up to the stated errors; these are the ideal leading amplitudes; a finite-radius compact-source field still has its Gamma/r² remainder, even if a dipole-replacement error happens to vanish. The identity $n\times(n\times e_3)=n(n\cdot e_3)-e_3$ with $n\cdot e_3=\cos\theta$ and the Pythagorean identity give $|n\times(n\times e_3)|=|\sin\theta|$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]). (b) Clause (d) of the theorem gives the limit $\mu_0/(16\pi^{2}c)\int|n\times V|^{2}d\sigma$ with $V=p''$; substituting $p''$ and using $|n\times p''|^{2}=|p''|^{2}\sin^{2}\theta$ yields the displayed density. Its integral uses $\int_{S^2}\sin^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})du=2\pi\cdot(4/3)=8\pi/3$ by [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](a) with $f(u)=1-u^{2}$; multiplying $\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)/(16\pi^{2}c)$ by $8\pi/3$ gives $\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)/(6\pi c)$. (c) The average uses $\int_0^{2\pi/\omega}\cos^{2}(\omega u)du=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$: substitute $v=\omega u$ or exhibit the antiderivative $\tfrac{u}{2}+\tfrac{\sin(2\omega u)}{4\omega}$ and evaluate at the endpoints by the fundamental theorem ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]); multiplying the mean value of $\cos^{2}$ by the coefficient gives the displayed result. (d) states the scope; no measured or fitted quantity appears, and the period average is explicitly in retarded time. For (e), choose a nonnegative smooth compact cutoff positive on a ball, normalize by its strictly positive finite Lebesgue integral, and scale that unit-mass bump to have support inside B_a ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]]) and eta by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Continuity is rho_t=-p_eta' dot grad sigma and div J=p_eta' dot grad sigma. Integration by parts with zero boundary gives integral rho0 and integral y_i rho=p_eta_i integral sigma=p_eta_i. Therefore [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] constructs the actual fields; [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] gives their moment identities and complete finite-radius and flux errors, not an exact D0 premise for a time-varying harmonic current. Integrating the absolute error over one selected period gives the claimed average-error bound.
